note: xmlParseEndTag2() (parser.c) checks whether the current input matches the still-open tag's name via `xmlStrncmp(ctxt->input->cur, ctxt->name, tlen)` and then, on a match, indexes `ctxt->input->cur[tlen]` to look for the closing '>' -- neither read is preceded by any check that at least tlen (respectively tlen+1) bytes remain before ctxt->input->end. A crafted end tag near EOF makes both reads walk past the end of the parser's input buffer (heap-buffer-overread).

traces.message: xmlStrncmp(ctxt->input->cur, ctxt->name, tlen) : reads up to tlen bytes from the input cursor with no check that tlen bytes remain before ctxt->input->end
ctxt->input->cur[tlen] : reads one more byte past that, still with no bounds check
